verdict.rationale: Lorikeet documents its own deterministic and natural-language workflows in which the agent takes actions through APIs. It also documents guardrails that screen incoming messages and responses and can block, rewrite or escalate, which is a rule-and-action pattern applied to message events. However, no evidence describes a general user-defined event-trigger rule engine; the outbound scheduling cadences are time-based, not event-based. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of configurable event triggers (e.g., ticket created or status changed) mapped to automatic actions, rule-condition authoring details, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: The agent takes action through your APIs and MCP servers inside natural-language and deterministic workflows

Incoming messages pass a prompt-injection classifier and bad-actor checks, while response guardrails screen what the agent says for grounding and policy, with the ability to block, rewrite or escalate.
Build, edit, and deploy workflows using natural language
